title: Lasers Used to Chill, Instead of Heat

image.attribution: red_hat. Red hat at de.wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
University of Washington researchers say they used a laser to turn hot water into cool water.

Five engineers from the university are the first in the 50-year history of the laser to refrigerate liquids under normal conditions with light beams.

The group used a simple approach to the experiment. Lasers are known for producing hot temperatures. The University of Washington says they “… ran the laser phenomenon in reverse.”

The discovery has a future in the computer and medical fields.

The cool laser concept can also be used in manufacturing, telecommunications.

The group has an interest in hearing from businesses or scientists who may have everyday applications for the cool laser.
